name: ocr_assist
description:
Language description:
Read text from the current image.

Real helper:
_call_ocr_assist(...)

Key outputs:
- `ocr["text"]`: OCR text result
- `ocr["image"]`: OCR visualization image
- `ocr["meta"]`: structured OCR metadata

Short example:
ocr = _call_ocr_assist()
print(ocr.get("text", ""))
result = ocr["image"]
usage_notes: Use the real helper name `_call_ocr_assist`. OCR often provides both useful text and a useful visualization image.

name: rotate_image
description:
Language description:
Rotate the current image to correct orientation or align the target for easier reading.

Direct code capability:
No helper is required; write the rotation directly with PIL.

Key patterns:
- 90 degrees clockwise: `result = image.rotate(270, expand=True)`
- 90 degrees counter-clockwise: `result = image.rotate(90, expand=True)`
- 180 degrees: `result = image.rotate(180, expand=True)`

Short example:
result = image.rotate(270, expand=True)
usage_notes: Use this when the image, chart, document, or label is clearly misoriented. Keep `expand=True` so the rotated image is not clipped.

name: flip_image
description:
Language description:
Flip the current image horizontally or vertically when the scene is mirrored or upside down.

Direct code capability:
No helper is required; use PIL transpose operations directly.

Key patterns:
- Horizontal flip: `result = image.transpose(Image.FLIP_LEFT_RIGHT)`
- Vertical flip: `result = image.transpose(Image.FLIP_TOP_BOTTOM)`

Short example:
result = image.transpose(Image.FLIP_TOP_BOTTOM)
usage_notes: Use this when text, axes, or object layout indicates the image is mirrored or upside down.

name: resize_image
description:
Language description:
Resize the current image to enlarge a small target or normalize it before the next inspection step.

Direct code capability:
No helper is required; resize directly with PIL.

Key patterns:
- Explicit size: `result = image.resize((new_w, new_h))`
- Keep aspect ratio manually when needed by computing the new size first

Short example:
width, height = image.size
result = image.resize((width * 2, height * 2))
usage_notes: Use this when the whole image or crop is too small to inspect comfortably. Keep the resized output as the new working image.

name: adjust_brightness
description:
Language description:
Adjust image brightness to reveal dark or washed-out details before the next inspection step.

Direct code capability:
No helper is required; use `ImageEnhance.Brightness` directly.

Key patterns:
- Brighten: `result = ImageEnhance.Brightness(image).enhance(1.4)`
- Darken slightly: `result = ImageEnhance.Brightness(image).enhance(0.8)`

Short example:
result = ImageEnhance.Brightness(image).enhance(1.4)
usage_notes: Use moderate factors first. This is useful when text or object boundaries are hard to see because the image is too dark or too flat.

name: adjust_contrast
description:
Language description:
Adjust image contrast to make faint text, boundaries, or local structure easier to inspect.

Direct code capability:
No helper is required; use `ImageEnhance.Contrast` directly.

Key patterns:
- Increase contrast: `result = ImageEnhance.Contrast(image).enhance(1.8)`
- Reduce contrast slightly: `result = ImageEnhance.Contrast(image).enhance(0.9)`

Short example:
result = ImageEnhance.Contrast(image).enhance(1.8)
usage_notes: This is one of the most common cleanup operations before OCR or close visual inspection. Prefer moderate factors such as 1.2 to 2.0.

name: adjust_sharpness
description:
Language description:
Adjust image sharpness to make fine text or edges more legible before the next inspection step.

Direct code capability:
No helper is required; use `ImageEnhance.Sharpness` directly.

Key patterns:
- Sharpen: `result = ImageEnhance.Sharpness(image).enhance(1.8)`
- Reduce oversharpening: `result = ImageEnhance.Sharpness(image).enhance(1.2)`

Short example:
result = ImageEnhance.Sharpness(image).enhance(1.8)
usage_notes: Use this when the crop is slightly blurry or soft. Prefer moderate sharpening over aggressive artifacts.

name: manual_box
description:
Language description:
Draw a box on an image using explicit pixel coordinates.

Real helper:
_call_manual_box(x1, y1, x2, y2, ...)

Key outputs:
- `box["image"]`: boxed visualization image
- `box["meta"]`: box-related metadata

Short example:
box = _call_manual_box(120, 80, 260, 180, label="target")
result = box["image"]
usage_notes: Use `_call_manual_box` exactly by name. Coordinates are pixel coordinates on the current selected input image, so check that image's width and height before choosing the box.

name: manual_crop
description:
Language description:
Crop a local region using explicit pixel coordinates.

Real helper:
_call_manual_crop(x1, y1, x2, y2, padding=0, ...)

Key outputs:
- `crop["image"]`: cropped image
- `crop["meta"]`: crop metadata

Short example:
crop = _call_manual_crop(120, 80, 260, 180, padding=4)
result = crop["image"]
usage_notes: Use `_call_manual_crop` exactly by name; do not shorten it to `manual_crop`. Coordinates are pixel coordinates on the current selected input image, so check that image's width and height before choosing the crop.

name: ground_box
description:
Language description:
Ground a text-described target and return a boxed image.

Real helper:
_call_ground_box(text_prompt, ...)

Key outputs:
- `box["image"]`: grounded box visualization image
- `box["text"]`: helper text feedback
- `box["meta"]`: grounding metadata

Short example:
box = _call_ground_box("price tag")
result = box["image"]
usage_notes: Use `_call_ground_box` exactly by name. `text_prompt` works best as a short visual target phrase such as an object name or short noun phrase. Long prompts or relational descriptions can make grounding unstable.

name: sam_mask
description:
Language description:
Ground a text-described target and return a highlighted mask image.

Real helper:
_call_sam_mask(text_prompt, ...)

Key outputs:
- `mask["image"]`: mask visualization image
- `mask["text"]`: helper text feedback
- `mask["meta"]`: mask metadata

Short example:
mask = _call_sam_mask("hanging tag", multimask_output=False)
result = mask["image"]
usage_notes: Use `_call_sam_mask` exactly by name. `text_prompt` works best as a short visual target phrase. Long prompts or relation-heavy descriptions can make the selected mask unstable.

name: dino_crop
description:
Language description:
Ground a text-described target and return one or more cropped regions.

Real helper:
_call_dino_crop(text_prompt, max_crops=1, padding=0, ...)

Key outputs:
- `crop["image"]`: primary crop image
- `crop["images"]`: all returned crop images
- `crop["text"]`: helper text feedback
- `crop["meta"]`: crop metadata

Short example:
box = _call_ground_box("serial number")
crop = _call_dino_crop("serial number", max_crops=1, padding=4)
result = crop["image"]
usage_notes: Use `_call_dino_crop` exactly by name. `text_prompt` works best as a short visual target phrase. Long prompts or relational descriptions can crop the wrong region. If multiple crops are returned, the final `result` must still be a single image.

name: blur_bg
description:
Language description:
Keep a grounded target clearer while blurring the background.

Real helper:
_call_blur_bg(text_prompt, ...)

Key outputs:
- `focus["image"]`: background-blurred image
- `focus["text"]`: helper text feedback
- `focus["meta"]`: blur-related metadata

Short example:
focus = _call_blur_bg("label")
result = focus["image"]
usage_notes: Use `_call_blur_bg` exactly by name. Mainly useful when clutter hurts inspection.

name: manual_depth
description:
Language description:
Measure the depth of an explicit pixel region on the full image.

Real helper:
_call_manual_depth(x1, y1, x2, y2, stat="median", vis_mode="overlay", padding=0, label=None, ...)

Key outputs:
- `depth["image"]`: full-image visualization with the region box and depth label
- `depth["text"]`: depth conclusion for that region
- `depth["meta"]`: structured region depth statistics

Short example:
depth = _call_manual_depth(120, 80, 260, 180, stat="median", label="target")
print(depth["text"])
result = depth["image"]
usage_notes: Use `_call_manual_depth` exactly by name. Coordinates are pixel coordinates on the current selected input image, so check that image's width and height before choosing the region. Prefer this when coordinates are already known and you want a stable region-depth estimate.

name: ground_depth
description:
Language description:
Ground a text-described target, pick one detection, then measure that detection region's depth on the full image.

Real helper:
_call_ground_depth(text_prompt, detection_index=0, box_threshold=0.35, text_threshold=0.25, stat="median", vis_mode="overlay", padding=0, label=None, ...)

Key outputs:
- `depth["image"]`: full-image visualization with the selected detection and depth label
- `depth["text"]`: grounding plus depth conclusion
- `depth["meta"]`: selected detection info and region depth statistics

Short example:
depth = _call_ground_depth("person", detection_index=0, stat="median")
print(depth["text"])
result = depth["image"]
usage_notes: Use `_call_ground_depth` exactly by name. `text_prompt` works best as a short visual target phrase. Long prompts or relational descriptions can make the chosen detection unstable. Prefer this when the target location is unknown but you want a single grounded detection plus its depth.

name: count_assist
description:
Language description:
Count text-described instances in the current image and return a count visualization.

Real helper:
_call_count_assist(text_prompt, confidence_thresh=0.23, visualize="heatmap", ...)

Key outputs:
- `count["image"]`: count visualization image
- `count["text"]`: helper text feedback
- `count["meta"]["count"]`: predicted count
- `count["meta"]`: structured count metadata such as boxes and scores

Short example:
count = _call_count_assist("car")
print(count["meta"].get("count"))
result = count["image"]
usage_notes: Use `_call_count_assist` exactly by name. Prefer this when the task is to estimate how many instances of a category appear in the image.
